'''''Iris boissieri''''' (also known as the '''yellowbeard iris'''), is a species in the genus ''[[Iris (plant)|Iris]]'', it is also in the subgenus [[Iris subg. Xiphium|Xiphium]]. It is from Europe, mainly Spain and Portugal. It has blue-purple (or deep purple) flowers with a yellow beard.

==Description==
It flowers in June.<ref name=Lynch>Lynch, Richard{{Google books|grvYTul5CSUC|The Book of the Iris|page=161}}</ref> It normally has only one flower per stem.<ref name=European>James Cullen, Sabina G. Knees, H. Suzanne Cubey (Editors) {{Google books|CkxWrDqtWLQC|The European Garden Flora Flowering Plants: A Manual for the Identification|page=259}}</ref> The flower is blue-purple (or deep purple),<ref name=European/> with a yellow<ref name=cassidy/> or orange beard.<ref name=Lynch/> It grows between 30 and 40 cm tall. The leaves appear in spring.<ref name=cassidy/>

It is the only bearded iris in the 'Xiphion' section.<ref name=cassidy>{{cite book |last1=Cassidy |first1=G.E.| last2=Linnegar |first2=S.|date=1987 |edition=Revised |title= Growing Irises|location=Bromley |publisher=Christopher Helm |pages=144–145 |isbn=0-88192-089-4 }}</ref>

== Taxonomy==
It is also known as the 'yellowbeard iris'.<ref name=american/>

Named after [[Pierre Edmond Boissier|Edmond Boissier]] (a Swiss botanist 1810-1885).<ref>{{cite book |last=Stearn |first=William |year=1972 |title=A Gardenerer's Dictionary of Plant Names |location=London |publisher=Cassell |isbn=0-304-93721-5 }}</ref>

In 1877, Mr A.W. Tait (from [[Porto]], Portugal) sent the bulbs to [[Michael Foster (physiologist)|Sir Michael Foster]] who grew them in the UK. It was first described in 1885 by Portuguese botanist [[Julio Augusto Henriques]] in ''Boletim da Sociedade Broteriana'' Vols. 1-28.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iris boissieri Henriq |url= https://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=321632| publisher=apps.kew.org| access-date=29 July 2014 }}</ref>

It was also described by Mr Foster in 'The Gardeners' Chronicles' of 1887, vol. ii. page38.<ref name=american>{{Cite web|title=(SPEC) Iris boissieri Henriques | url=http://wiki.irises.org/bin/view/Spec/SpecBoissieri| publisher=wiki.irises.org (American Iris Society)|access-date=29 July 2014}}</ref>
It was then described in [[Curtis's Botanical Magazine]] 7097 in 1890 again by Mr Foster.<ref name=Lynch/>

It was verified by [[United States Department of Agriculture]] and the [[Agricultural Research Service]] on 4 April 2003 and then updated on 2 December 2004.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate=6 July 2015}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Iris boissieri'' is [[native plant|native]] to Europe.<ref name=grin/>

===Range===
It was originally found in the [[Serra do Gerês]] (a mountain range in [[Portugal]]), Northwest [[Spain]],<ref name=cassidy/><ref name=grin/> within ([[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]]).<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /><ref name=species>{{cite web|title=Species of the Day – Iris boissieri|date=9 December 2012| url=https://natureology101.wordpress.com/2012/12/09/species-of-the-day-iris-boissieri/ |publisher=natureology101.wordpress.com| access-date=29 July 2014 }}</ref>

===Habitat===
It likes to grows in rocky shallow soils,<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> at an altitude of {{convert|2000|-|3000|ft}} above sea level.<ref name=american/>

==Conservation==
It was on the 1997 [[IUCN Red List]] of Threatened Plants.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /><ref>Kerry Scott Walter, Harriet J. Gillett (Editors) {{Google books|XIL9adYYeSIC|1997 IUCN Red List of Threatened Plants|page=678}}</ref> It was listed on the ''European Red List of Vascular Plants'' in 2011 as Data Deficient (DD).<ref>{{cite web |first=Melanie |last=Bilz |first2=Shelagh P. |last2=Kell |first3=Nigel |last3=Maxted |first4=Richard V. |last4=Lansdown |title=European Red List of Vascular Plants |date=2011 |url=https://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/species/redlist/downloads/European_vascular_plants.pdf |publisher=ec.europa.eu (Publications Office of the European Union) |access-date=29 August 2015}}</ref>

Very few plants (less than a 1000) were found in Spain in 2004 and less than a 10,000 plants were found in Portugal. Also these numbers were gradually going down as well.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

''Iris boissieri'' was listed on Annex IV of the [[Habitats Directive]] (of the [[European Union]]). It was therefore assessed as 'Critically Endangered'.<ref name=species/>

==Cultivation==
It is best grown in a [[bulb frame]].<ref name=cassidy/>

There is a specimen in the [[Kew Herbariu]]m, collected by Winkler in 1876.<ref name=american/>
There is also a specimen in the 'Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques' in [[Geneva|Genève]], collected in 1899.<ref>{{cite web|title=History: Type of Iris boissieri Henriq. [family IRIDACEAE]| url=http://plants.jstor.org/specimen/g00164604 |publisher=plants.jstor.org |access-date=29 July 2014 }}</ref>

===Hybrids and cultivars===
Emily Jean Stevens (1900–1967) was a hybridiser of ''Iris boissieri'' and ''[[Iris juncea]]'' in the 1950s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stevens, Emily Jean| url=http://www.teara.govt.nz/en/biographies/5s43/stevens-emily-jean| publisher=www.teara.govt.nz|access-date=29 July 2014 }}</ref>
